title: Roadmap Launch Readiness - Incident Review & Q2 Handoff
summary: Quick incident review for last week's rollout, impact assessment, check launch readiness and Q2 handoff items. Plan remediation items and owners, confirm security sign-offs and final rollout gating criteria.
action_items: Marcus Chen - Produce full postmortem draft and timeline (due 2026-05-21)
Elena Garcia - Run additional load tests on Dedicated pools and share results (due 2026-05-19)
Samir Patel - Add canary/fallback policy to deployment config and test rollback automation (due 2026-05-18)
Jordan Lee - Share launch checklist and final go/no-go criteria with execs (due 2026-05-17)
Ravi Menon - Confirm KMS integration and provide audit logs for security review (due 2026-05-20)
next_steps: Send incident timeline + logs to product and security (Jordan)
Schedule follow-up with security to sign off on KMS/SOC2 artifacts (Elena)
Prepare customer-facing incident note template (Alice & Jordan)
Book engineering deep-dive for performance optimization next Tuesday
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-14 | Start: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 45 minutes | Location: Zoom | Organizer: Jordan Lee
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: ok everyone, thanks for joining the roadmap launch readiness and incident review, let's kick off, we have about 45 minutes
00:22 Priya Shah: yeah i'll start with a very quick recap, last thursday's rollout saw a latency spike around 11:42, some requests hit 2 to 3x expected p95
00:41 Marcus Chen: and we saw the dedicated pool run out of burst capacity, autoscaler didn't bring up nodes quick enough, i think there was also a kv cache pressure issue
01:05 Elena Garcia: mhm, the k v cache, sometimes transcriber writes that as K-V cache, but yes the eviction threshold was high and combined with big seqs caused memory pressure
01:30 Jordan Lee: can you repeat the memory bit, elena? was that a kernel-level OOM or GC?
01:45 Elena Garcia: more like the runtime memory footprint spiked, not a kernel OOM, but the process started thrashing, reclaimed then restarted the worker, so we saw retries
02:10 Samir Patel: there was also a config mismatch — one of the quantization profiles on the new model variant wasn't applied in prod, so CPU paths were heavier
02:35 Priya Shah: ok so root causes are autoscaler latency + cache eviction policy + model config mismatch, good to list those
02:55 Marcus Chen: mitigation we did was rollback to previous model variant and increased bursting, that reduced requests to normal within ~12 minutes
03:15 Jordan Lee: did rollback trigger our runbook automatically or was it manual?
03:30 Marcus Chen: manual — we haven't wired full rollback automation to the canary yet
03:50 Elena Garcia: that should be a priority for the launch, right, full automated fallback to compatible variant
04:05 Jordan Lee: agreed, we need canary and fallback, and signal thresholds, like error rate and p95 latency, and a hard abort if tail latencies cross x
04:30 Priya Shah: security asks — we need audit logs and KMS attestations, SOC2 reviewers want last 12 months of key rotations and RBAC mappings
04:55 Ravi Menon: on that, we confirmed KMS integration with the private deploy last week but need to collect the rotation logs and share with security
05:20 Samir Patel: small note, the telemetry can be noisy, some metric names were different in the new agent, so dashboards glitched, we'll normalize
05:55 Jordan Lee: good catch. also we should test Dedicated pool scaling under sustained traffic, not just spike tests
06:15 Marcus Chen: i'll own a stress test plan, run it against dedicated pools with a realistic mix of prompt lengths and KV cache patterns
06:40 Elena Garcia: i'll look at autoscaler tunables and see if we can reduce scale-up latency while avoiding overprovisioning
07:05 Priya Shah: timeline for launch — we want a soft launch next Monday, but given incident we may want to delay by one week to ensure fixes
07:30 Jordan Lee: what's the minimum gating criteria to ship? can someone list top 5?
07:50 Priya Shah: 1) rollback automation + canary, 2) autoscaler latency below threshold, 3) KMS/audit logs in place, 4) postmortem + mitigation plan, 5) SLO check with redwood optimize suggestions applied
08:25 Samir Patel: on 5) we need to ensure batching and quantization recommendations are packaged into the deploy, maybe an optimize profile
08:55 Marcus Chen: i'll coordinate with research to pin quantization profiles and validate accuracy regressions
09:20 Jordan Lee: ok, action items — we'll capture those and owners after this, but also, security wants a checklist for SSO and RBAC
09:45 Ravi Menon: SSO is already configured for staging, we need to replicate prod mappings and test SCIM sync
10:05 Elena Garcia: can we also add a run of the incident response playbook? there were a couple of handoffs that were messy
10:25 Priya Shah: yes, runbook rehearsal, and a shorter war room for launch day
10:45 Jordan Lee: status check from each owner, marcus?
11:00 Marcus Chen: postmortem draft will be ready by next week, due 2026-05-21, will include timeline, root cause, and regression checks
11:25 Samir Patel: i'll prototype the fallback automation by monday and run unit tests, target 2026-05-18
11:45 Elena Garcia: load tests by 2026-05-19, i'll share raw results and a summary
12:05 Jordan Lee: security, ravi?
12:20 Ravi Menon: KMS logs + rotation proof by 2026-05-20, and i'll set up a meeting with security reviewers for 2026-05-22
12:45 Priya Shah: design and customer comms — alice will prepare an incident note template and a customer-facing FAQ
13:10 Alice Wu: yes, i'll draft and share by 2026-05-17
13:30 Jordan Lee: ok let's quickly run through the launch checklist items and owners — we'll put everything in the shared doc
13:55 Priya Shah: on canary thresholds, propose p95 < 200ms and error rate < 0.5% for 10 minutes to advance
14:20 Samir Patel: sounds reasonable, but behavior under long sequences might need different thresholds
14:40 Marcus Chen: we'll layer sequence-length bucketing into canary analysis
15:05 Elena Garcia: one more item — monitoring alert pages were too noisy during incident, need to tune dedupe and escalation policy
15:30 Jordan Lee: noted. final thing, we need to prep the executive one-pager for the board tomorrow, include outage impact, customer impact, and mitigation timeline
15:52 Priya Shah: i'll take the one-pager
16:05 Jordan Lee: great. recap of next steps — i'll send the incident timeline and shared checklist, owners will execute items, follow-up in one week
16:30 Multiple: thanks all, bye
16:38 [END]
